_note: FIRST baseline for this profile. 075 recorded it in-file only, so Article VIII §2's ±5% budget had nothing to compare against; 082 T046 (FR-022(a) / SC-012 / K10) creates it. Release build, --benchmark_min_time=0.5s, 4 runs. READ THE per-benchmark spread fields before treating any single figure as a gate: this profile's run-to-run spread is 9-18%, so a ±5% budget is NOT resolvable on one run and must be evaluated against `measured_release_us_runs`.
_before_side_caveat: The pre-change (T002) figures below are n=1 — a single run captured before implementation, with no spread recorded. Their variance is therefore unbounded and the before/after deltas MUST NOT be read as precise. What the data does support is the weaker, sufficient claim: no regression. The FIX44 / FIX50SP2 deltas are NEGATIVE (faster) by 34-44%, which is outside this profile's measured 9-18% run-to-run spread in the same direction, so Article VIII §2's no-regression obligation is met without needing the exact magnitude to be trustworthy. The speed-up itself is NOT root-caused and is deliberately not claimed as a 082 improvement.

The timing column on THIS row is process warm-up, not a signal; only sizeof_B is.

benchmarks.name: BM_TableView_BuildFix42
benchmarks.verdict: NEW ROW — no pre-change counterpart EXISTS, and that is the finding, not a gap in the data
benchmarks._why_no_before: Pre-082, FIX 4.2 registered ZERO repeating groups (L-063-1), so as_table_view() did no group work for it and the row was absent from this profile. This row measures work that did not previously exist; it cannot regress against anything.
benchmarks._group_bits_note: The heap half of FR-022(a). sizeof(table_view) is unchanged (row 1), but `group_bits_` is a std::vector<std::uint64_t> that goes EMPTY -> (max registered no_tag >> 6) + 1 words per table_view COPY on FIX40/41/42. Measured 7 words = 56 B for FIX 4.2. Derived in-bench from the public group_first_field() accessor, not from the private member, so the figure is reproducible.

_predicted_cost_not_observed: T046's task text predicted a slowdown on EVERY dictionary — including the byte-identical ones — because the per-field group test goes from one enum compare to an O(log G) binary search over `groups_` (G = 507 on FIX50SP2, ~9 comparisons). That cost is NOT observable at this profile's granularity: FIX50SP2 and FIX44 both measured faster than the n=1 pre-change figure. Recorded as measured rather than as predicted, per Article VIII's 'asserting any leg unmoved instead of measuring it is non-conforming'.
